subject: Clarify productization & output rights in MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Emma Kline <emma.k@novumhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@novumhealth.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form - initial redlines

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the meeting earlier — attached are Novum's redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. High level concerns:
- Output ownership: Novum expects explicit language that customer retains exclusive rights to output (derivatives/productization) created from their content.
- Training & feedback: we need opt-in consent for model training; if Redwood uses any outputs to improve models, Novum requires anonymization and a carve-out for productization rights.
- Attribution & escrow: Novum wants a short auditability clause and an option to escrow models if training occurs.

We're trying to keep the contract timeline tight (legal wants signed before 11/05). Can you confirm Redwood's stance and whether these are deal-breakers?

Attachments: Novum_MSA_Redlines_20261010.docx (docx)

Best,

Team — forwarding Novum's redlines. They flagged output ownership and training consent as the two biggest points. Quick ask: can legal propose language that preserves Novum's productization rights while giving Redwood a narrow, non-exclusive telemetry/feedback license for service improvement that is: aggregated, de-identified, and non-commercially redistributable?

Items to triage: 
1) Output ownership: Novum wants 'exclusive rights' language. We should confirm whether we can accept customer ownership for outputs generated from their data in the hosted product, but need a carve for safety/abuse detection.
2) Training opt-in: propose an Order Form flag — default is opt-out; enterprise customers can opt-in with explicit terms and pricing.
3) Feedback license: recommend timebox (e.g., 24 months), non-identifiable aggregation, and an SOW for any model retraining that uses customer data.

If legal can draft a redline that: a) limits training to opt-in only, b) allows Redwood to use aggregated telemetry for quality, and c) preserves customer's right to productize outputs, we can present it back to Novum as a compromise.

Laura/Jordan — please add anything I'm missing re: procurement or commercial risk. Karthik, can you take a first pass at proposed language by Monday? Novum expects a response within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA + Order Form - initial redlines

Grace — thanks for the flag. I took a look and drafted a proposed redline (attached: rw_proposal_redline_20261011.docx) that attempts a middle ground. High-level summary of our proposal: 

- Output language: customer retains ownership of Outputs (defined as model-generated content that directly originates from customer's input), but Redwood retains rights to use derivative signals for abuse/safety and to comply with legal obligations. We explicitly exclude "Output" used for commercial redistribution by Redwood.

- Training & feedback: Default behavior: Redwood will not train on customer content unless the customer opts in on the Order Form. For customers who opt-in, Redwood will require express written consent to use customer content for model training; any such use will be subject to technical de-identification and an SOW that defines scope and compensation.

- Feedback license: We propose a limited, perpetual (or time-limited?) license for telemetry and aggregated feedback solely for service improvement. Suggest limiting to 24 months after termination unless customer opts for longer during negotiation. If Novum insists on opt-out semantics, we can add an explicit billing uplift for opt-in training.

Open questions for legal/commercial: 
* Is 24 months enough for improvement use cases? (Pros: bounded exposure; Cons: may reduce long-term model improvement.)
* Escrow: Novum's escrow ask for models triggered by training is non-standard for us — propose a fallback: enhanced auditability and a runbook for retraining events instead of escrow.

I'll attach inline redlines. If you want, Laura I can walk through these with procurement on Monday.

Attachments: rw_proposal_redline_20261011.docx (docx), redline_summary.xlsx (xlsx)

Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form - initial redlines

Emma — thanks for sending these over and for the timeline. We've reviewed and put together a proposed compromise (key points below). I'm copying Karthik and Laura so Legal/Procurement are aligned.

Summary of Redwood's compromise: 
- Outputs: Novum retains ownership of Outputs produced from their content. Redwood will not assert ownership over customer-generated outputs. We will, however, retain the right to use non-identifiable derivatives for safety and to meet legal obligations.
- Training: Training on Novum customer content will only occur if Novum explicitly opts in on the Order Form. For any opt-in training, Redwood will commit to de-identification, a scoped SOW, and a one-time training fee to compensate for compute and engineering resources.
- Feedback license: Redwood requests a limited license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement for up to 24 months after termination; this will not include redistributable models.
- Escrow alternative: instead of escrow, Redwood will provide a retraining runbook, attestations, and the option for enhanced audit access during any retraining event.

Next steps: 
1) Karthik will send an inline redline (attached) with the exact language by end of day.
2) If Novum is happy in principle, can we schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call on Wednesday 10/14 to close the outstanding items?

If anything above is a hard stop for Novum, let us know ASAP — we'd like to preserve the signing window but can escalate if required.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
